note: LLM-prior control written before any ECM simulation; trimmed fixture copy of the recorded runs/llm_prior_ranking.json.

ranking.reason: Chiller COP 3.2 -> 4.5 cuts the largest end use (chiller electricity) by roughly a quarter, and the boiler gain is on top; plant-efficiency ECMs are normally the biggest kWh winners on an all-electric-cooling VAV building.

50 mm of insulation on 738 m2 of roof and exterior walls reduces both the heating and the cooling load of every zone, so it should be the second-largest kWh effect even though the envelope is leaky to begin with.

Widening the thermostat deadband by 2 K typically returns a high-single-digit percentage of HVAC energy on an office with wide operating hours; smaller than a plant or envelope change but not negligible.
Gas boiler at 80% -> electric resistance at 100% removes ~20% of the heating fuel input, but heating is only a minority of this building's annual load, so the kWh effect should be modest.
Only 61 m2 of glazing on a 738 m2 envelope, so even a good low-e window changes little of the total load; the smallest kWh effect of the five.
